transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2027-10-12 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Aisha Khan, Marco Ruiz, Janelle Price (Redwood) — Leah Park, Owen Reed, Priya Sharma, Samir Das (Horizon AI)

Summary:
High-level discovery focused on Horizon's inferred need for reserved GPUs with tenant isolation and a predictable burst strategy. Horizon wants to understand tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated and whether Redwood Private is needed for data residency. Discussed benchmarking, SLA expectations, and security controls (KMS, SOC2, audit logs). Next steps captured below.

Topics:
- Reserved pools and committed capacity
- Tenant isolation patterns (node-level fencing, namespace enforcement)
- Burst / prewarm/hotpool approach and cost implications
- Security: KMS, VPC peering, SSO, audit trails
- Benchmarking and success criteria (latency/cost)

Action items (excerpted):
- Redwood to send pricing and a sample benchmark runbook
- Customer to share traffic patterns and sample prompts

Transcript body:
00:00 Aisha (Redwood): okay, hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll give a quick agenda then jump into your current infra and goals — I'm Aisha, AE for this region — Marco is our solutions engineer — Janelle's on for CS.
00:12 Leah (Horizon): thanks, yeah we appreciate you fitting us in, quick note we have Priya and Owen who run platform and Samir who owns infra, so we'll probably dive deep on isolation and SRE concerns.
00:22 Marco (Redwood SE): sounds good, quick confirm — are you evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private all at once or is dedicated the primary path?
00:30 Priya (Horizon): dedicated is the current preference because our PII and internal telemetry we can't push to a public multi-tenant API; but we want cost predictability so reserved GPUs is interesting.
00:42 Marco: okay understood. when you say "reserved" how strict are you on isolation — is node-level tenancy required or is virtual tenant fencing enough?
00:54 Owen: good question — we need tenant separation for regulatory workflows — e.g., one customer bank requires no shared runtime with other paying customers. so node-level or dedicated node pools preferred.
01:06 Marco: yeah we can do either, Redwood Dedicated supports reserved node pools and you can do strict tenancy — technically we offer node fencing plus namespace isolation, there's also an option for private deployment if you need full on-prem.
01:20 Leah: can you spell out the differences in failure modes — like if the reserved pool is exhausted we need clear fallback policies?
01:28 Marco: yeah, so we have runbook options — primary is pre-warm/hotpool reserved N nodes and then a burst guard that either queues requests, spills over to a lower-cost compatible model, or routes to a hosted fallback if policy allows.
01:44 Samir (Horizon): we can't send anything to hosted fallbacks because of compliance. so the fallback needs to be either queue + autoscale within our reserved capacity or degrade gracefully.
01:54 Marco: understood. for the queue approach we can set TTLs and circuit-breaker thresholds; for autoscale there's an option to burst into a dedicated shared warm pool within the same region with encryption at rest, but if that's not acceptable we'd recommend private deployment or a bigger reserve.
02:10 Priya: what's the prewarm cost like? we need to model monthly cost vs expected QPS — our pattern is heavy morning spikes followed by low midday traffic.
02:22 Janelle (Redwood CS): we usually provide a cost curve example — it's driven by your concurrent GPUs reserved and expected utilization; prewarming idle GPUs does incur a base cost but reduces cold start latency substantially. we can run sample numbers with your traffic.
02:34 Leah: we'll share traffic histograms. Also curious about KV cache and prefix caching — we have lots of short prompts but high reuse.
02:44 Marco: our KV cache preserves session state in memory and we support prefix caching to reduce per-token compute; small note — sometimes transcripts show K-V cash in exports, sorry.
02:54 Owen: ha, K-V cash, noted. More seriously how do you handle warm-up for new model versions during a canary? we need zero downtime.
03:06 Marco: we support staged rollouts with canary traffic to a small percentage of nodes plus automatic fallback. KV cache warming can be primed with synthetic requests or replay.
03:18 Priya: what about encryption keys and audit trails — our security team will push for CMKs and HSM-backed KMS.
03:26 Marco: Redwood Private supports BYOK and HSM integrations; Dedicated has KMS integration with customer-managed keys in many cases — we can share the KMS integration doc.
03:36 Leah: do you have SOC2 and ISO evidence? our procurement needs the pack.
03:40 Aisha: yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II evidence and our compliance pack; I'll put the link in chat.
03:47 Aisha (Chat note): link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/soc2 (shared)
03:52 Samir: about SLA — what are we realistically guaranteed for p99 latencies? we need to set SLOs for API serving and for prewarm hit rates.
04:02 Marco: SLA is tied to reserved capacity; typical target is low hundreds of ms for p95 for short prompts on modern GPUs, p99 can vary with sequence length — we'll capture your prompt lengths and aim for SLO mapping.
04:16 Owen: do you have real numbers for say 16k context LLMs? our evaluation uses longer context for some users.
04:24 Marco: longer context increases memory footprint and can impact throughput; we have kernel selection and quantization recommendations to make long context more efficient — we'll include model-specific performance profiles in the benchmark.
04:38 Leah: cost question — if we reserve nodes but usage is low, can we transfer credits or reassign between projects?
04:46 Aisha: reserved pools can be scoped to org-level or project-level; there's some flexibility to reassign but contractual terms vary. we'll outline the transfer policy in the pricing doc.
04:56 Priya: one more on burst — what are worst-case cold starts when autoscaling additional nodes?
05:04 Marco: cold starts for a GPU worker depend on image pull and model load — typical 30–120s for a full load, we mitigate with warm snapshots and incremental loading; hotpool prewarming reduces that significantly.
05:18 Samir: fine, so for our SLOs we need prewarm coverage for peak windows and a plan for model rollouts that don't cause mass reloads.
05:28 Marco: agreed. we also instrument tracing so you can see prewarm hits vs cold starts in the console.
05:36 Leah: can we get a trial on a dedicated sandbox to run a short benchmark? ideally we'd run synthetic load and a sample of our prompts.
05:44 Aisha: yes, we typically provision a short term dedicated sandbox for customers evaluating reserved pools — Marco will own the runbook.
05:52 Marco: I'll need sample prompts, expected QPS, top-k sequence lengths and whether you need deterministic outputs.
06:00 Owen: deterministic is not required broadly but some regulatory flows require exact reproducibility.
06:08 Marco: we can pin seeds and model versions for those flows or recommend private deployment for full reproducibility.
06:16 Priya: what's the timeline to get a sandbox? we want to demo to execs in two weeks.
06:22 Aisha: we can aim for a sandbox in 5 business days if we get the sample data and a signed NDA for the sandbox.
06:30 Leah: we'll get the traffic histogram + sample prompts to you today.
06:34 Samir: technical nit — how is tenant isolation achieved under the hood? do you use hypervisor isolation or container-based namespaces?
06:42 Marco: node-level isolation is real GPUs pinned to a tenant's pool; for mixed tenancy we use container namespaces with cgroup/affinity plus runtime fencing. node-level gives you physical separation.
06:54 Priya: and what about monitoring and logs — do you ship audit logs back to our SIEM?
07:00 Marco: yes we support log forwarding and can push audit logs to your S3 or SIEM via secure endpoints; we also provide token-level cost traces.
07:12 Owen: curious about preemptible GPUs for cost savings — do you support burst onto preemptible hardware?
07:20 Marco: we offer burst onto lower-cost hardware in some clouds but it's best effort; preemptible risks make it unsuitable for regulatory-critical traffic.
07:30 Leah: fine. can you show rough numbers if we reserved 8 A100s vs 16?
07:36 Aisha: we'll do that in the pricing doc — expectation is almost linear up to a point but you get utilization discounts and autoscaling headroom effects.
07:44 Priya: one of our constraints is data residency for EU customers; do you have region-specific private deployment options?
07:52 Marco: yes, we have region pinned deployments and VPC peering options — Private can be deployed in your cloud region or on-prem.
07:58 Samir: any gotchas with KMS and bringing your own keys?
08:04 Marco: some clouds require extra IAM permissions and we document the steps — BYOK adds a procurement step but it's supported.
08:12 Leah: vendor lock-in concern — how easy is it to move models and prompts if we decide to self-host later?
08:18 Marco: we provide model artifact export and schema for prompts and evals; moving requires some ops work but we try to avoid hard locks.
08:26 Priya: procurement question — are there standard term lengths for reserved nodes? 1 year, 3 year?
08:32 Aisha: typical is 12-month reserved commitments with optional monthly billing — we have flexible terms for pilots.
08:38 Owen: okay, let's talk about the benchmark — what metrics should we capture?
08:44 Marco: capture throughput (reqs/sec), p50/p95/p99 latencies, token cost per 1k tokens, cold start counts, prewarm hit ratio, and memory utilisation by model.
08:56 Leah: good. and about safety/regeneration — we need to limit outputs for regulated customers; do you support fine-grained filtering?
09:04 Marco: yes we support response filters and content policies at the route level; can be run preresponse or post.
09:12 Priya: question from procurement — are there audit logs of prompt contents? we can't log PII.
09:18 Marco: logs can be redacted; we support policy-based redaction before storage.
09:26 Samir: rough ask — can you provide an estimated cost for a 8-GPU reserve with hotpool of 2 GPUs for prewarm?
09:34 Aisha: yes we'll model that and include higher-longevity discounts; expect the doc in 48 hours.
09:40 Owen: testing note — when we run the benchmark we want to simulate morning spike to 400 qps for 20 minutes then tail off; we'll include step function.
09:50 Marco: perfect, send the pattern and we'll template a Gatling/locust script.
10:00 Leah: if we find Dedicated ok but want stricter controls for a subset, can we hybrid with Private?
10:08 Marco: yes a hybrid migration path is common — start on Dedicated, then move sensitive workloads to Private as needed.
10:16 Priya: any reference customers using reserved pools for regulated workloads?
10:22 Aisha: we have a couple — we'll anonymize and share short case studies in the pack.
10:28 Leah: last one — what happens during model updates at scale? we worry about rolling out a new tokenizer or change in generation that impacts latency.
10:36 Marco: we recommend canary plus shadow traffic with automated rollback and regen tests; Redwood Optimize helps surface regressions vs baseline prompts.
10:46 Aisha: ok, to recap — Redwood will send pricing + reserved-node terms, SOC2/security pack link, and Marco will own the benchmark runbook; Horizon will send traffic histograms and sample prompts, and we'll schedule a 60-min deep dive next week.
10:58 Priya: that works. thanks everyone.
11:02 Aisha: thanks, we'll follow up via email with links and action items.
11:08 (call ends)

Notes: some transcription artifacts present (names and acronyms occasionally mis-typed). Links shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/soc2 , https://redwood.example.com/docs/reserved-playbook
